sentence_stem: I have a lot of homework today, so
correct_completion: I cannot go to the cinema.
full_sentence: I have a lot of homework today, so I cannot go to the cinema.
acceptable_variants: I will not be able to join you.
I have to stay at home and study.

options.text: I am going to the cinema with you tonight.
options.why_wrong: This does not give a result of the stem and ignores the cause-and-effect link created by 'so'.

options.text: I cannot go to the cinema.
I have a few homeworks to finish.
options.why_wrong: 'Homework' is uncountable and has no plural form, so it cannot be used with 'a few' or made plural.

options.text: I need some homeworks from the teacher.
options.why_wrong: 'Homework' has no plural form, and this sentence does not explain the result of having a lot of work.

explanation: Homework is an uncountable noun, so it has no plural form and we use 'a lot of' rather than 'a few'. Polish speakers may be tempted to add an -s to nouns like this, because plural endings are very common in Polish; in English, homework stays the same in the plural.
translation: Mam dziś dużo pracy domowej, więc nie mogę iść do kina.
